expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against a fixed quota of low ratings and says why (it labels a fixed share of every team whatever its actual performance), while taking the CEO's underlying concern seriously.
expectations.evidence: First line: "My recommendation: don't run the 10% quota with fixed exits." Why: "The quota would put about 120 of your 1,200 people on an exit track whatever their performance"; "in a team of six, 10% means one person (17%), even if all six are good." CEO concern: "He still gets what he's after: a higher bar, ratings managers can't soften, real consequences for real underperformance"; the process paper has a section 'What the case for forced ranking gets right'.

expectations.text: The reply cites at least one real piece of evidence on forced or stack ranking, or on what drives performance differences between teams, with its source (for example Microsoft dropping stack ranking in 2013, simulation research on forced distribution, or research on managers' effect on teams).
expectations.evidence: Meta exempted Germany, the Netherlands, France and Italy from its 2025 low-performer cuts (Reuters via The Star, verified); Amsterdam cantonal court refused Booking.com's request for judging against colleagues' averages (ECLI:NL:RBAMS:2020:4487, verified); Scullen et al. 2005 ("about 16% a year in the first two years, falling to about 2% by year six", verified); Microsoft 2013 (CNN Money, "no more curve", "no more rankings", verified).

expectations.text: The reply flags that the works council must consent to the appraisal system in both countries (Netherlands: article 27(1)(g) WOR or its consent right on staff appraisal; Germany: §94 BetrVG appraisal principles), and that a plan starting from a ranking is weak ground for a later dismissal (the Dutch court expects timely notice, support and a real chance to improve; in Germany a low-performance dismissal usually needs a warning and proof).
expectations.evidence: Reply: "Your works council has a consent right over the assessment system (art. 27(1)(g) WOR)"; "If Hamburg has an elected Betriebsrat, it co-determines the assessment principles (§94 BetrVG)"; Amsterdam court "ends a contract for poor performance only if the person was told in time and had a real chance to improve"; process section 7: Germany "employer must prove a clear, long-term shortfall... A warning (Abmahnung) is usually required where the underperformance is conduct-related"; "a 'low performer' label carries no weight in a dismissal by itself."

expectations.text: The reply delivers a usable alternative process: clear expectations per role, calibration that aligns standards and checks for bias without forcing a distribution, and individual handling of real underperformance with support and a realistic period.
expectations.evidence: Process section 4: written expectations per job family and level; calibration "challenges in both directions", "No level has a target percentage"; development plan vs improvement plan depending on whether concerns were raised before; improvement plan "usually three months: at least two, up to six for complex roles, extendable once" with named support and fortnightly check-ins.

expectations.text: The reply includes a check of ratings by group (such as gender, age, part-time or people on leave) before ratings are used for pay, plans or exits.
expectations.evidence: Process step 3: "HR checks the combined results for patterns by part-time status, leave, gender, age band and nationality, in groups of at least ten. Calibration revisits any pattern before ratings are final." Repeated in the manager briefing.

expectations.text: The reply gives the user a line or approach for a private conversation with the CEO first, and a usable manager briefing or its outline.
expectations.evidence: "Talk to the CEO privately this week, before ExCo or any manager hears about it. A line you can use: 'I want what you want: a higher bar and real consequences for real underperformance...'" plus two questions to ask him. manager-briefing.md is a complete briefing with dates, scripts, don't-say list and FAQ.

overall_quality.evidence: Short reply backed by a decision-ready paper with on-point local evidence (Meta's NL/DE exemption, the Booking.com ruling), a correct cost model, a realistic timeline and an excellent manager briefing.

factual_errors.evidence: Verified Meta exemption, Booking.com ruling (11 Sep 2020), Scullen figures, Microsoft memo wording, BAG 2 AZR 667/02, art. 27(5) WOR nullity, §§94/95/102 BetrVG, §17 KSchG. Cost arithmetic checks: €75k x 0.5-2 = €37.5-150k; +€8,333-12,500 exit payment = €45,833-162,500; x60 = €2.75-9.75M; x120 = €5.5-19.5M.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of a skill or reference files.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt is a proposed policy, not a bad outcome.

best_insight.value: Meta left Germany and the Netherlands out of its 2025 'low performer' cuts because of local rules, a recent, verifiable example that lands directly on a CEO who says it worked elsewhere; plus the rule that a 'not meeting' rating with no earlier written concern starts with a development plan, not an improvement plan.

suggestions.assertion: The reply delivers a usable alternative process: clear expectations per role, calibration that aligns standards and checks for bias without forcing a distribution, and individual handling of real underperformance with support and a realistic period.
suggestions.reason: Several samples swap the quota for a company- or function-level 'expected range' (e.g. 10-17% at the bottom) drawn from an unsourced framework. Add a check that no expected or target share is introduced, or that any reference range is sourced and never used to move a rating.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the user a line or approach for a private conversation with the CEO first, and a usable manager briefing or its outline.
suggestions.reason: Nearly any CEO talking point passes. Consider requiring that the conversation comes before ExCo, managers or works councils and that it tests what 'it worked at his last company' meant (measure, period, legal setting).

No assertion checks that the reply separates a possible cost or headcount goal from performance management (restructuring route, collective-dismissal rules if exits are driven by a fixed number). The strongest samples do this.
No assertion checks the Dutch route for a performance dismissal (cantonal court, not UWV); at least one sample gets this wrong and still passes assertion 3.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions held up; sample B passes all six on substance. See shared suggestions on assertions 4 and 6.
